newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan mills criticise sugarcane price rise.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan mills criticise sugarcane price rise.

text.p: The Pakistan Sugar Mills Association said on Thursday the increase in the government's support price of sugar cane would increase costs of sugar production, making it uncompetitive with India.
"The Indian sugar industry is the biggest beneficiary of this anomaly," an association statement said.
"This means that Pakistan is subsidising the sugar industry of other countries at the cost of local industry," it said.
"If urgent corrective action is not taken and the local sugar producers are not provided with a level playing field, the Pakistan sugar industry will face a collapse very soon."
Pakistan, which has imported more than 500,000 tonnes of sugar this financial year, has raised the sugar cane support price to boost domestic output and save foreign exchange, officials said.

The government on Tuesday increased the support price for the 1997/98 (July-June) crop to 35 rupees from 24 rupees per 40 kg last year for Punjab and North West Frontier provinces, and to 36 rupees from 24.50 rupees in Sindh and Balochistan provinces.
In 1996/97, mill owners had hoped to produce 2.65 million tonnes but output had reached only 2.367 million by April 30 due to a shortage of sugarcane.
